newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CGIP buys Daimler's Cap Gemini stake for 1.4 bln DM. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CGIP buys Daimler's Cap Gemini stake for 1.4 bln DM. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG subsidiary Debis said on Thursday CGIP, the holding company for French software maker Cap Gemini, had agreed to buy the German group's 24.4 percent stake in Cap Gemini for 1.4 billion marks in cash.
(Corrects headline and first paragraph to make clear CGIP and not Cap Gemini bought shares from Daimler)

"CGIP accepted our share offer last evening. It means we will have finished the transaction no later than July 28," Debis chief executive Klaus Mangold told reporters during a high-level meeting of eastern European political and business leaders in this alpine city.
"We will have round about 1.4 billion marks in cash."

Mangold said Daimler would cancel an originally planned convertible bond issue and pay holders of the notes 104 percent (Corrects from four percent) of their original investment in cash. The notes were to have a maturity of four-and-half years and to be exchanged into shares of Cap Gemini at the option of investors.
"We will pull off the issue since CGIP had the first right of refusal (on the shares). We have foreseen this as one of the scenarios," Mangold said.

Daimler, Germany's biggest industrial group, said last month it would pull out of Cap Gemini because of differing strategic focuses and because a U.S. Bank Holding Company Act hindered Cap Gemini's business there.
In a statement released in Salzburg, Daimler also said Cap Gemini would return its 19.6 percent stake in Debis unit Debis Systemhaus.
